turns_text: [SEG0001] person_1 (NURSE): Come on through, Mrs. Hale. I grabbed vitals before the doctor steps in, so we are not starting from zero.
[SEG0002] person_2 (PATIENT): Thank you. I am sorry to be seen on such short notice. I hope the schedule is not too disrupted.

[SEG0003] person_1 (NURSE): Blood pressure is one hundred eight over seventy two, heart rate ninety eight, temperature ninety nine point one, oxygen sat ninety eight percent, and respirations sixteen. Her mouth looked a bit dry to me.
[SEG0004] person_3 (DOCTOR): Thank you, Karen. Mrs. Hale, I'm Dr. Okonkwo. Sit wherever is comfortable. What has been happening?
[SEG0005] person_2 (PATIENT): We were at my niece's wedding on Saturday, Doctor. Since then I have had diarrhea, and I vomited as well. It has been quite disruptive.
[SEG0006] person_3 (DOCTOR): A wedding meal, then this. Did the diarrhea start that same night, or later?
[SEG0007] person_2 (PATIENT): Sunday morning, as I recall. So two days. I woke and went directly to the bathroom.
[SEG0008] person_4 (FAMILY_MEMBER): No, you were up Saturday night. I heard you in the hotel bathroom around midnight. That's three days of it, not two.
[SEG0009] person_2 (PATIENT): I... well, perhaps I am misremembering the hour. I had thought Sunday. I do not want to insist if you heard me.

[SEG0010] person_3 (DOCTOR): Let me say it back. One of you has diarrhea from Sunday, about two days, the other from Saturday night, about three. I will not force a single start time. Roughly two to three days is as tight as we can honestly get.
[SEG0011] person_4 (FAMILY_MEMBER): And she's not the only one. Her sister called, the groom's uncle, a couple of the cousins. Same table, same salmon, all of them down with it.
[SEG0012] person_3 (DOCTOR): Several people from that table are ill. Do you remember what you ate?

[SEG0013] person_2 (PATIENT): I chose the salmon. There was also a cream pasta and a chocolate cake. I had a small piece of cake. The reception was lovely, actually, the string quartet was... well, that is neither here nor there.
[SEG0014] person_3 (DOCTOR): We'll leave the quartet. Vomiting, how many times, and has it stopped?
[SEG0015] person_2 (PATIENT): Twice yesterday evening. The last time was around ten. I have not vomited today.
[SEG0016] person_4 (FAMILY_MEMBER): She was dry-heaving over the sink this morning. Nothing came up, but it wasn't pretty.
[SEG0017] person_2 (PATIENT): That is true, nothing came up. I would not call that a vomit, if we are being precise.
[SEG0018] person_3 (DOCTOR): So vomiting stopped after about ten last night, and there was a dry heave this morning with no vomit. Nausea still with you?
[SEG0019] person_2 (PATIENT): Yes. It comes and goes. I have not felt like eating.
[SEG0020] person_3 (DOCTOR): How many times have you had diarrhea? A number, if you can.
[SEG0021] person_2 (PATIENT): I am embarrassed to say I lost count. Perhaps six, or it may have been eight, since yesterday morning. After lunch I simply stopped tallying. It is watery.
[SEG0022] person_3 (DOCTOR): Watery, somewhere around six to eight, not a firm count. Any blood in it, or a black, tarry look?
[SEG0023] person_2 (PATIENT): No. Nothing like that. No blood.
[SEG0024] person_3 (DOCTOR): Did you feel feverish, or check a temperature at the hotel?
[SEG0025] person_2 (PATIENT): Mm, I suppose I felt a little warm in the evening. Sometimes, not really. I never put a thermometer to it, so I should not claim a fever.
[SEG0026] person_3 (DOCTOR): I won't write down a fever from that. Too hedged. Cramping?
[SEG0027] person_2 (PATIENT): Yes, low in the belly. Moderate, I would say. It eases somewhat once I have been to the bathroom. It does not double me over.
[SEG0028] person_3 (DOCTOR): Lightheaded at all? Dry mouth?
[SEG0029] person_2 (PATIENT): A little lightheaded if I stand up quickly. And my mouth is dry, even though I have tried to sip water. I am not usually one to complain.
[SEG0030] person_4 (FAMILY_MEMBER): She sipped, like, twice. I bought ginger ale at the gas station and it's still in the car, mostly full.
[SEG0031] person_3 (DOCTOR): Noted, intake has been light. Before I examine you, what have you taken for this?

[SEG0032] person_2 (PATIENT): I took Imodium, those little green and gray capsules, the anti-diarrhea medicine. My sister, who used to work in a clinic, texted me not to take it if other guests were sick. I took it anyway. I was mortified, sharing one bathroom.
[SEG0033] person_3 (DOCTOR): Loperamide, against your sister's advice. How many, and what strength?
[SEG0034] person_2 (PATIENT): The box says two milligrams. This morning I took two capsules. Or, well, actually, it may have been one, and then I took another around noon. I am not certain.
[SEG0035] person_3 (DOCTOR): So the strength on the box is two milligrams, and the number of capsules is maybe one, maybe two. I will not pretend we verified that. Please do not take any more today.
[SEG0036] person_2 (PATIENT): I understand. I will stop them. I hope I have not made matters worse.
[SEG0037] person_3 (DOCTOR): You haven't done anything we can't walk back. What medicines do you take on a regular basis?
[SEG0038] person_2 (PATIENT): For my blood pressure I take a little white water pill. I have never managed to remember the proper name. Ordinarily it is once in the morning.
[SEG0039] person_3 (DOCTOR): The water pill, name unknown. Have you actually been swallowing it each day through this?
[SEG0040] person_2 (PATIENT): Mm, I suppose. Sometimes, not really. Yesterday is a blur. I would not swear to it.
[SEG0041] person_4 (FAMILY_MEMBER): The pill box doesn't lie. Today's compartment is still full, so she missed at least this morning. I think the bottle says hydro-something. Don't quote me.
[SEG0042] person_3 (DOCTOR): I won't quote you. Neither of you can name it, so it stays the little white water pill until I see the bottle. Missing a day or so is information, not a disaster.
[SEG0043] person_2 (PATIENT): I have had high blood pressure for about five years. My own physician has called it well controlled, generally.
[SEG0044] person_3 (DOCTOR): High blood pressure, about five years, ongoing. Any antibiotics in the last few weeks? Any other pills?
[SEG0045] person_2 (PATIENT): No antibiotics. No other regular medicines. I did buy some travel mints, but that is hardly relevant.
[SEG0046] person_3 (DOCTOR): Any drug or food allergies?
[SEG0047] person_2 (PATIENT): None that I am aware of.
[SEG0048] person_4 (FAMILY_MEMBER): They did a colonoscopy, um, three years back? Said it was fine. She hates when I bring up bowels at parties, but here we are.

[SEG0049] person_2 (PATIENT): Yes, about three years ago, and I was told it was fine. Separately, at my physical last spring, they said my kidney function was borderline. No new medicine was started. I was not given a number, or if I was I did not retain it.

[SEG0050] person_3 (DOCTOR): Let me reflect that back. Colonoscopy about three years ago, reported as fine, no details. A blood test last spring, kidney function called borderline, no numeric result in front of us. I will not treat borderline as a lab value I can use today.

[SEG0051] person_3 (DOCTOR): I'm going to examine you now. Lips and tongue are dry, and skin turgor is slightly reduced. Abdomen is soft, with mild tenderness low down, no guarding and no rebound. Heart sounds are regular and the lungs are clear.
[SEG0052] person_1 (NURSE): I can do lying and standing pressures if it'd help. I didn't, earlier.

[SEG0053] person_3 (DOCTOR): I don't think we need orthostatics this visit. With a pulse of ninety eight, pressure one oh eight over seventy two, and a dry mouth, this is mild dehydration. Not severe. She's perfusing fine.
[SEG0054] person_2 (PATIENT): Is there a name for what this is? I would prefer a plain answer, even if it is incomplete.

[SEG0055] person_3 (DOCTOR): I'll think out loud, and I want you to hear the limits. It could be a foodborne illness from the wedding salmon, since several people at that table are sick, or just as easily a viral gastroenteritis from a crowded reception. I am not going to conclude this is bacterial, and I will not stamp it food poisoning as a settled diagnosis. What I will say is an acute gastroenteritis, with those two possibilities side by side, and we will see how you do before leaning further.
[SEG0056] person_4 (FAMILY_MEMBER): So you're not starting an antibiotic.

[SEG0057] person_3 (DOCTOR): Correct, not today. Let's see what the next couple of days show before any test. I am not ordering a stool study now. If you are not clearly better in forty eight hours, or if you see blood, or you cannot keep fluids down, then we send a stool sample.
[SEG0058] person_2 (PATIENT): And in the meantime, what would you have me do?

[SEG0059] person_3 (DOCTOR): Fluids first, small frequent sips of an oral rehydration solution. If packets are a nuisance, water with a pinch of salt and a little sugar will do, though the solution is better. Ginger ale only counts if you truly drink it. Eat small bland portions when the nausea allows.
[SEG0060] person_2 (PATIENT): I can manage the small sips. I am not certain we have the packets at home.
[SEG0061] person_3 (DOCTOR): Stop the Imodium. Hold the little white water pill until you are keeping fluids down, then restart the same one. Bring the bottle in so we can name it.
[SEG0062] person_2 (PATIENT): Stop the Imodium. Hold the water pill until I am drinking properly, then restart it, and bring the bottle. I shall write that down.
[SEG0063] person_4 (FAMILY_MEMBER): I'll put the bottle in her purse tonight. The label's rubbed, that's half the problem. We had this same argument at the pharmacy in March.

[SEG0064] person_3 (DOCTOR): Come back, or call the clinic, if you are not better in two days. Sooner than that if you faint, if the vomiting returns and you cannot sip, if there is blood, or if you stop passing urine.
[SEG0065] person_2 (PATIENT): If I may ask, is the dry mouth the part that worries you most?
[SEG0066] person_3 (DOCTOR): It's the piece that tells me you are a little behind on fluid, not a sign of something separate. Replace the fluid and that should ease.
[SEG0067] person_4 (FAMILY_MEMBER): We've got the grandkids Saturday, which is chaos, but I'll keep them out of her hair. Sorry, not medical.
[SEG0068] person_2 (PATIENT): Please excuse the aside. I will follow the instructions carefully. You have been very clear, and I appreciate it.
[SEG0069] person_1 (NURSE): I'll print the rehydration sheet and walk you to the desk. Downstairs pharmacy stocks the packets, if you want them on the way out.

[SEG0070] person_3 (DOCTOR): If the diarrhea settles before those forty eight hours, you do not need the stool test, and you do not need to come back just to say you improved. A phone call is enough if you are unsure.
[SEG0071] person_2 (PATIENT): Understood. Thank you, Doctor. Thank you, Karen.

spec.situation: Diarrhoea and vomiting after a trip or a wedding meal; others at the event are ill; patient counts bowel movements loosely; takes loperamide against advice; mild dehydration signs; stool test conditional; advice on fluids.
features: colloquial_drug_names: medicines referred to by colour, purpose or brand ('the water tablet', 'Crocin', 'my sugar tablets', 'the purple inhaler'); the name is recorded as said, the normalized name only if it is clear.
ambiguous_answer: an answer that sounds like yes but is really 'maybe' ('mm, I suppose', 'sometimes, not really'); recorded with uncertainty or not at all, never as a firm fact.
test_result_recalled: the patient reports an old test or result ('they said it was borderline'); recorded as reported history/investigation only as far as said, not as a confirmed value.

doctor_thinks_aloud: the doctor lists possible causes or says what they will not conclude yet. Only record a clinical assessment if the doctor actually states a leading or differential impression; 'let's see what the tests say' is not an assessment.

bad.reason: Medication and morning frequency for blood pressure supported, but current use is uncertain and then advised to hold.
bad.text: little white water pill (frequency=once in the morning, indication=high blood pressure, status=currently_used, reported_by=patient)

omissions.text: Several other wedding guests from the same table were also ill after eating, including the patient's sister, the groom's uncle, and cousins; salmon at that table was specifically implicated as a possible shared exposure.
The patient denied recent antibiotic use in the last few weeks.
The patient reported no other regular medicines besides the blood pressure 'water pill.'
Vomiting was documented as onset 'yesterday evening,' but the transcript only states it occurred twice yesterday evening and stopped around 10 PM; a dry heave occurred this morning without emesis.
Abdominal cramping was additionally described as 'does not double me over,' which is a severity descriptor rather than a separately asked negative finding.
The doctor explicitly decided not to obtain orthostatic vital signs at this visit.
The doctor explicitly stated that antibiotics were not being started today.
The doctor stated no stool study was being ordered now, and to watch the next couple of days before any test.

Return/call instructions included 'come back, or call the clinic' if not better in two days; if diarrhea settles before 48 hours, no stool test and no return visit are needed, and a phone call is enough if unsure.
Decreased urine output/anuria was included as a red-flag follow-up instruction: seek care sooner if she stops passing urine.
